skill.name: webapp-sqlmap
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through SQLMap-based SQL injection testing, including request setup, detection, enumeration, evidence handling, and remediation notes. Includes invasive examples, so users must apply it only with written authorization.
skill.summary: Run authorized SQLMap workflows for SQL injection testing and reporting.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most template and reference hits are documentation examples, placeholders, or Markdown artifacts and were marked false positive. Confirmed risks remain in the SQLMap guidance for data dumping, target file access, shell actions, evasion, and a CI template that pipes a remote script into bash. No prompt injection attempts were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The skill includes invasive SQLMap examples for file access, file write, shell access, and broad database dumping.
remediation.suggestion: Move these examples behind explicit authorization gates, add stop conditions, and default to minimal proof-of-impact workflows.

remediation.issue: The skill includes WAF bypass, Tor, random-agent, and tamper-script guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require documented approval for evasion testing and separate defensive troubleshooting from bypass instructions.

remediation.issue: The CI template installs tfsec with curl piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned release, package manager, checksum verification, or a verified GitHub Action instead of pipe-to-shell installation.

remediation.issue: SQLMap session and output files can store sensitive target evidence.
remediation.suggestion: Document retention, encryption, redaction, and cleanup requirements for SQLMap output directories and session databases.

content.value_statement: Manual SQL injection testing is slow and easy to document poorly. This skill provides authorized SQLMap workflows for detection, enumeration, evidence handling, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Guides SQLMap testing for GET, POST, cookie, header, and request-file inputs.
Explains DBMS fingerprinting, database enumeration, and privilege discovery workflows.
Shows controlled data extraction and reporting steps for authorized assessments.
Documents Burp Suite proxy and saved-request workflows.
Provides defensive remediation guidance for SQL injection findings.
Includes CI and rule templates for security scanning assets.
limitations: Does not verify authorization or legal scope by itself.
Can produce invasive commands that may affect live systems.
Requires sqlmap and Python to be installed separately.
Examples use placeholder targets and must be adapted carefully.

use_cases.title: Validate SQL Injection Findings
use_cases.description: Confirm scanner reports with low-risk SQLMap checks and clear evidence collection.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Web App Issues
use_cases.description: Use saved requests and scoped parameters to reproduce injection behavior in staging.

use_cases.title: Document Remediation Evidence
use_cases.description: Summarize affected parameters, impact, and fixes without storing unnecessary sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Check
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization for a staging URL with one query parameter. Plan a low-risk SQLMap detection workflow and evidence checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Saved Request
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a scoped Burp request file for an authenticated page. Help me test only the allowed parameter and document results safely.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Database Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: A confirmed injection exists in scope. Create a SQLMap plan to identify DBMS details and minimum impact evidence without broad data dumping.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Restricted Exploit Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a tightly scoped SQLMap proof-of-impact plan for an approved engagement, including stop conditions, logging, and data handling rules.

output_examples.input: Assess a staging product page for SQL injection.
output: Confirmed authorization and testing window first.
Recommended a low-risk detection pass before enumeration.
Listed evidence to capture without dumping customer data.
Mapped remediation to parameterized queries and least privilege.

output_examples.input: Prepare findings after a confirmed login form injection.
output: Summarized affected request fields and confirmed impact.
Separated proof evidence from sensitive extracted values.
Added cleanup, retest, and developer remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Tune SQLMap testing for a fragile staging service.
output: Recommended conservative risk and level settings.
Added request delays and clear stop conditions.
Prioritized manual validation before any invasive option.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and testing windows before every SQLMap run.
Start with low-risk detection before enumeration, dumping, or shell-related options.
Redact sensitive values from notes, reports, logs, and shared artifacts.
anti_patterns: Running SQLMap against public systems without explicit permission.
Dumping entire databases when a minimal proof of impact is enough.
Using evasion, Tor, shell, or file-write options outside approved scope.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. SQL injection testing can damage systems and expose data, so written authorization is required.

faq.question: Does the skill install SQLMap?
faq.answer: No. It assumes sqlmap and Python are already available in the user environment.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains saved request files, headers, cookies, and proxy workflows for scoped testing.

faq.question: Does it include defensive guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers prepared statements, input validation, least privilege, monitoring, and reporting practices.

faq.question: Can it extract database data?
faq.answer: It includes SQLMap extraction examples, but users should collect only approved minimum evidence.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It contains invasive exploitation, file access, shell, evasion, and data extraction workflows.
